clue.text: Describing where William Wordsworth wandered?

parts.note: the phrase repeats its opening W sound over and over, so the clue itself is an example of the device it asks for

explanation.surface: A question about the route of the poet who wandered lonely as a cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sends you to the Lake District; the answer instead describes the words of the clue themselves, with their run of W sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Words starting with the same sound in close succession make a phrase of this kind, the poetic device of repeated initial sounds.

clue.text: Tempers turning hot and cold

definitions.meaning: to temper metal or glass is to toughen it by treatment
the process heats the material then lets it cool slowly

explanation.definitionFit: Metalworkers toughen glass or steel by heating then slowly cooling it, which is both the temper sense and the hot-and-cold sense.

clue.text: Throw back dead uncooked fish downwind

indicators.note: to throw back is to send the whole string of pieces the other way, so they are read in reverse

parts.note: uncooked food is raw
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler tosses a dead raw fish back into the water, downwind of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw back' turns the whole string round, so the fish ends up at the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side away from the wind is the side the wind blows toward, i.e. the downwind side in sailing terms.

clue.text: Arouse bird getting full sex returned with energy

indicators.note: the bird gets the other letters into itself, so it contains them

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: returned means the words full and sex are read backwards

parts.note: full can mean all, the whole of it
it is a common slang word for sex
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A racy line about a bird getting all the sex it wants with renewed vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the full-plus-sex string round to give TILLA, which sits inside the bird; 'with energy' adds the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite or stimulate someone, especially sexually, is a synonym of arouse.

clue.text: First woman attached to army unit, it's official

indicators.note: attached to puts the woman's name joined on after the army unit

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army unit
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman is the first to join an army unit, and it is now official.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a local magistrate or manorial overseer in England, so an official in the broad sense.

clue.text: Judas, informer embracing one in high place

indicators.note: in places the informer group inside the high place

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: embracing means the informer word wraps round the numeral

parts.note: a rat is slang for an informer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Judas, the informer, holds an exalted place.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name is a byword for a betrayer.

clue.text: Criminal laid up in hollow

indicators.note: in puts the sick word inside the empty word

parts.note: hollow, as in a hollow boast, means vain
someone laid up is ill in bed

explanation.surface: A criminal has been laid up in some hollow, hiding out.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or crook is a criminal; the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Gossip from British bird about soaps

indicators.note: about means the British bird goes round the soap word

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey
lathers is a verb meaning soaps or froths up

explanation.surface: Gossip from a British bird about TV soap operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaps' suggests TV dramas, but here it is a verb: to work up a foam. The answer is a rare dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks at length without much sense, a chatterbox or gossip.

clue.text: Liberal Tory leader after leftie taking in English

indicators.note: after puts the Tory's first letter at the end
taking in means the Russian revolutionary's name contains the abbreviation

parts.note: Lenin was the Bolshevik leader, a famous leftie

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political sketch: the Tory leader follows a leftist who takes in the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party, but it is the definition: tolerant or permissive.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal or permissive attitude is a merciful, indulgent one.

clue.text: Commissioned sailor steered on empty Exxon…

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the oil company's name is removed, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
led means guided or steered

explanation.surface: A commissioned sailor took the helm on an empty Exxon tanker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just places the sailor and steering after the empty Exxon in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be commissioned for a task is to be authorised or empowered to do it.

clue.text: Coppers dash off base, no time for administration

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
to pen a note is to dash it off

indicators.note: no time means one T is removed from the base word

parts.note: a station is a base, such as a military base

explanation.surface: Police officers race away from base with no time for paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensation is the management or ordering of affairs, as in a divine or political dispensation.

clue.text: Labour's hunt to secure a victory

definitions.note: Labour's here reads as Labour is, so the definition is the noun labour

indicators.note: to secure means the hunt word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to trail is to follow or hunt

explanation.surface: The Labour Party is hunting for a victory at the election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is not the party but hard toil; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard toil or painful effort is labour; the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Catches faithless partner holding it back

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read in reverse
the two words hold the answer letters inside their run

explanation.surface: A betrayed spouse catches an unfaithful partner and holds it against them.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare someone in a trap is to catch them.

clue.text: Diminished support with Democrat ousting Liberal

indicators.note: ousting means the Democrat letter takes the place of the Liberal one

parts.note: an easel is a support for a painting

explanation.surface: Liberal support diminished when a Democrat ousted him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain that has lessened or abated is said to have diminished.

clue.text: Charlie stood around posh before Church affirmation…

indicators.note: before puts these letters ahead of the church abbreviation
around means the fool and the ran word go round the posh letter

parts.note: a Charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass
to stand for election is to run, so stood means ran
U means upper-class, posh
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fool stood for posh office before making a church affirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'charlie' is British slang for a fool; U for upper-class is a convention from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A positive declaration or pledge is an affirmation; the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Stood before

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Stood before (9)' is cut short: the blog's hint mentions a homophone of 'radiant' and a heavenly body, so words are missing

clue.text: …ceremony with bag, right, having final word

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like structure

indicators.note: having means the right abbreviation holds the final word inside

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer

explanation.surface: A ceremony continues with a bag, and someone with the right to have the final word.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious rite such as baptism or communion is a church ceremony.

clue.text: More like a bitch, paradoxically?

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog, yet a spiteful, bitchy person is described with a feline word

explanation.definitionFit: Spiteful remarks are called feline in English, so a more malicious person is described comparatively with the cat word.

clue.text: Zeppelin tune? Start to smoke joint!

parts.note: an air is a tune

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Led Zeppelin tune? Start smoking a joint!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zeppelin' suggests the rock band, but it is the German airship.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeppelin is the name of the rigid dirigibles built by Count Zeppelin.

clue.text: 'How's your father?', say religious groups

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: how's your father is British slang for sex

explanation.surface: A coy question, 'how's your father', is put to religious groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is a British comic euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups splitting from a larger church or faith are religious factions.

clue.text: Treatment for bad state of shock

definitions.text: Treatment for bad state of shock

parts.words: Treatment for bad state of shock
parts.note: shock here is a shock of hair, so the treatment is a wash for a messy head of hair

explanation.definitionFit: A hair wash is the remedy for an unkempt mop of hair.

clue.text: Six needed to win in Trivial Pursuit?

definitions.text: Six needed to win in Trivial Pursuit?

parts.words: Six needed to win in Trivial Pursuit?
parts.note: in the board game a player collects six coloured wedges, commonly called by a dairy name, to win

explanation.definitionFit: The coloured wedges in Trivial Pursuit are nicknamed after wedges of the dairy product, and six are needed to win.

clue.text: Acting fit, embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means the fit phrase wraps around the heart letter

parts.note: in trim means fit, in good shape
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: An acting role that is fit and embracing a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: An acting head is a temporary, stopgap one, the provisional sense.

clue.text: American university tries heart out for baseball gear

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: heart out means the middle of the word is removed, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: An American university tries its heart out in baseball gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchers' gloves in baseball are big padded gloves, the slang word for hands.

clue.text: Nibble ends in smallest getting most emaciated

indicators.note: in puts the outside letters inside the smallest word

parts.note: least is another word for smallest, as in not the least idea

indicators.note: ends means the first and last letters of nibble

explanation.surface: Nibbling at the smallest scraps leaves someone most emaciated.
explanation.definitionFit: The thinnest, most gaunt person is the one with least flesh, a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Record single with tenor taking the title

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is one, single

explanation.surface: A singer's record of a single, with the tenor taking the title role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' means T takes THE before it; I is 'single', not the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive name or nickname, such as the Great in Alfred the Great, is a title.

clue.text: Sort of painting done in one second

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the done word within one and second

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
past means done, over

explanation.surface: A sort of painting completed in a single second.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting technique with thickly laid paint is a sort of painting.

clue.text: Trousers pop undone around end of farce? Farcical

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the final letter
undone suggests the trousers come apart, so their letters are rearranged
end of means the last letter of farce

explanation.surface: Trousers popping undone at the end of a farce is farcical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' rearranges TROUSERS POP, which goes around E, the last letter of 'farce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd or ridiculous, as a farce is, is a synonym of farcical.
